processList.title: Processes
processList.empty: No processes with audio sessions found
processList.emptyHint: Play sound in the target app, then refresh
processList.stopAllConfirm: Click again to stop all routing
processList.multiSelectHint: Click to select; Ctrl+click to pick several and route them together

deviceVolume.valueLabel: Volume of {{device}}, relative to the loudest device, in percent
deviceVolume.hint: Attenuates this device relative to the loudest one in its group. Drag sideways, or scroll / press arrows for {{step}}% a time (hold Shift for ten); click to type an exact value
deviceVolume.inactive: Not applied right now: volume balancing only runs in multi-device duplication routes
deviceVolume.primary: The system plays this device directly, so software cannot attenuate it; its value anchors the group's loudest level

deviceDelay.hint: Drag sideways, or scroll / press arrows for {{step}} a time (hold Shift for ten); click to type an exact value
deviceDelay.syncOff: Latency sync is off, so these values are not applied; enable it in the settings
deviceDelay.inactive: Not applied right now: delay compensation only runs in multi-device duplication routes; a single-device route is played by the system directly
deviceDelay.primary: The system plays this device directly (the route's anchor); its value only shifts the alignment reference of the whole group

sourceLevel.valueLabel: Level this app gives the audio of {{process}}, in percent
sourceLevel.hint: Level this app gives this program's audio on the way to its devices, as a percentage: 100 leaves it as the program produced it, below attenuates, above amplifies. Drag sideways, or scroll / press arrows for {{step}}% a time (hold Shift for ten); click to type an exact value

deviceLatency.hint: Software-side latency only: the engine's pipeline for this device plus the endpoint's own reported stream latency. What a codec or a Bluetooth link adds on top is invisible to the app, so what you hear is later than this
deviceLatency.inactive: Nothing to measure: no engine is duplicating this device — a single-device route is played by the system directly
deviceLatency.primary: Not measurable: the system plays this device directly (the route's anchor), so there is no stream of ours to ask

settings.title: Settings
settings.autoRememberDesc: Remember each process's device routing and restore it automatically
settings.delaySyncDesc: Compensate faster devices to align with a slower (Bluetooth) one
settings.resetEndpointsDesc: Gives every program its own output device back, except the ones a route is using right now. A program an earlier version left fixed to a device ignores the system default until this is done.
settings.stopAllRoutesDesc: Returns every routed program to the system default at once. The programs a route is not using are left alone.
settings.closeToTrayDesc: The close button hides the window while every route keeps running, and the tray icon brings the window back. Turned off, closing quits the app and stops the routes with it.
settings.autostartDesc: Launches into the tray with no window at sign-in, so remembered routes are ready before you open anything.
settings.delayNote: Every device's delay is set against the app's audio; a route is applied in delay order, so the device the OS plays directly is the earliest one and becomes the alignment reference. On the main screen, drag the number under a device node, or scroll it. Delay and volume only apply in multi-device duplication routes; a single-device route is played by the system directly, with no engine in between.
settings.calibrationNote: Each device's latency is measured and shown under it on the main screen, but that figure is the software side only: what a codec or a Bluetooth link adds happens after the audio leaves Windows, and measuring it would take a microphone. This app does not ask for one, so that last stretch stays yours to place by ear — which the live number turns into a matter of seconds rather than guesswork.
settings.delayRangeDesc: Delays can be set within this ± range
settings.delayStepDesc: How much each − / + click changes; an exact value can also be typed
settings.sourceLevelsAlignDesc: Brings every program this app is duplicating that is playing up to the loudest one's level, in one action. One that is not making a sound has nothing to measure, so it is left exactly as it is.
settings.sourceLevelsNote: A program's level is the gain this app gives its audio on the way to the devices it is routed to: our own copy of the sound, after it was captured. It is not the program's own volume, and nothing Windows stores is touched by it. 100 leaves the program as it produced it, and anything above amplifies it.
settings.sourceLevelsNone: No program is being duplicated right now. A level only applies in a multi-device route — a route to a single device is played by the system directly.
settings.aboutDesc: Per-app audio routing for Windows — Rust talking to Windows Core Audio directly, no third-party executables.

startup.upgradeTitle: An earlier version ran on this PC
startup.upgradeBody: It may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you hit one, clear it with the button below; if not, there is nothing to do.
startup.upgradeBodyVersion: The last version to run on this PC was {{version}}, and it may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you hit one, clear it with the button below; if not, there is nothing to do.
startup.resetHint: This clears every program that is running now, including a device you set by hand in the volume mixer. A program that is not running keeps its device until it starts.
startup.resetDone: Cleared the fixed output device of {{n}} program(s).
startup.resetRemaining: {{processes}} could not be cleared — let it play a sound and try again.
startup.firstRunBody: Pick a program that is playing on the left, click a device on the right, then press the button in the middle and the sound moves there. Pick several devices to play on all of them at once. If a program ever stops following the devices you switch to in Windows, the reset in Settings releases it.
